items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Herman Chittison whom I had met some years before in Boston accompanying the comedian Stepan Fetchet.

ctx.x: Another musician and song writer that I had seen in New York who was now living in Paris was Spencer Williams who composed the famous "Basin Street Blues". I met the members of Willy Lewis's band that were not with him when I met him in the south of France. Joe Hayman played alto-sax and Frank "Big-Boy" Goodie, tenor and clarinet, who was really a big boy about 7 feet tall and must have weighed 280 pounds. He had also played cornet but eventually gave it up. Johnny Mitchell was the guitarist.

I think that Garnet had worked a short while with Willy and it did not go so well because Garnet was quite wild and flighty. So Willy had engaged Herman Chittison whom I had met some years before in Boston accompanying the comedian Stepan Fetchet.

One week after I had started playing at the Villa d'Este I was able to go from Place Pigalle to the Etoile or Arc de Triomphe with the bus and I had the feeling that I was learning more about the great city of Paris.
